text:
Ellen: Hey team — need a quick pointer for NimbusFinance (private VPC) observability. Where are their Prometheus remote_write endpoints and Grafana dashboards? Also curious how logs/traces are forwarded into our ingestion (OTLP?). @Sam @Mike

Sam: Hi — Grafana org id is 42. Dashboards are provisioned at https://grafana.redwood.internal/orgs/42/dashboards and the datasource name is `nimbus-prom`. We push a provisioning JSON during onboarding.

Mike: Prom remote_write endpoint is our receiver: https://prom-receiver.internal:9090/api/v1/write . Token stored in Secrets Manager. Example remote_write snippet we give to customers:
```
remote_write:
  - url: "https://prom-receiver.internal:9090/api/v1/write"
    bearer_token_file: /etc/secrets/nimbus_prom_token
    queue_config:
      max_samples_per_send: 2000
```

Jess: For logs we typically recommend Vector (customer side) forwarding to our OTLP/logs endpoint. Example sink: 
```toml
[sinks.otlp_logs]
  type = "otlp"
  inputs = ["source_logs"]
  endpoint = "https://logs-ingest.internal/v1/logs"
  compression = "gzip"
```
Traces -> OTLP at https://otlp-ingest.internal/v1/traces (TLS + mTLS optional).

Ellen: Thanks. Where do alerting rules live for Nimbus? Customer asked to tune memory_high from 90 -> 95 and maybe adjust the window.

Sam: Rules are in their infra repo under `infra/observability/alerts`. Link: https://git.redwood.internal/nimbus/infra/-/tree/main/observability/alerts . I can open an MR to change the threshold.

Jess: FYI 95 might mask real problems. Suggest raising threshold and increasing `for` to 10m, plus a separate OOM page. Proposed rule change: memory_high: `avg_over_time(node_memory_used_percent[5m]) > 95` -> change to 95 with `for: 10m` and add `severity: warning` before firing page. Also add runbook note.

deploy-bot: MR created by Sam: https://git.redwood.internal/nimbus/infra/-/merge_requests/57 — contains Prom remote_write docs + alert tweak. Deploy scheduled to canary on 2026-03-05T15:30Z.

Mike: Note: their VPC peers to our ingestion subnets. Make sure the route to 10.3.0.0/16 -> ingestion is present and security groups allow 9090/443.

infra-oncall: Confirmed peering and routes. Route table rt-0987 has the route to 10.3.0.0/16 and SGs allow the expected ports. No outstanding infra blockers.

Ellen: Perfect — I'll add these links to the customer handoff doc and ping customer success. Thanks all :thumbsup:
